post.name: Reminder about Rule #2: No politics
post.body:
**(edit 3/23/25: re-stickying this since we've gained a lot of new users in recent months)**


I just want to post a reminder that this is the general memes community, and we'd prefer for political memes to be directed to c/politicalmemes. 


Thanks, TPM

post.name: Alternative history: Tokyo monster explosion
post.body:
In 1954, the first Godzilla movie premiered, spawning a franchise and between 1954 and 1975, the so called Showa series of Godzilla movies were released. In this series, iconic monsters such as Mothra, King Ghidorah, mecha godzilla made their appearance. 

After The Terror of Mechagodzilla, the franchise was put on a hold for a few years. That was until in 1984 with The Return of Godzilla. As part of the new so called Heisei series, audiences were promised an entire new rooster of monsters. This began with the second movie Godzilla vs Biollante, with Biollante by far being the most conceptually creative and technically impressive monster that had yet to appear in a Godzilla movie. And indeed, it was according to a poll from 2014 the most popular Godzilla movie.

Unfortunately, Godzilla vs Biollante performed less than Toho had expected. And as a result, for the future movies in the Heisei series, almost all the monster featured had been featured in the Showa series, or were slight derivations thereof. 

So for the next round of movies, Godzilla fights:
- King Ghidorah
- Mecha King Ghidorah (almost a meta rehash of Mecha Godzilla)
- Mothra
- Evil Mothra (Battra)
- Mecha Godzilla
- Mecha Godzilla 2 (M.O.G.U.E.R.A, actually, from an unrelated monster movie)
- Godzilla himself, but with crystals protruding from his shoulders (Space Godzilla)
And of course, Destoroyah, which is the only other truly creative monster in this series.

This trend has mostly followed over to the next iteration in the Millenium series, and the new Reiwa series of movies, where Godzilla so far has once again fought King Ghidorah. 

To think, that if Godzilla vs Biollante had been a smash hit, every single movie in the Heisei series could have featured a new monster. And maybe even this trend would have followed into the Millennium and Reiwa era.
